invariant.note: width of its distance axis 0.75 A, not searched

topomer.note: 60 of 66 molecules can be cut at the framework

findings.text: 14 chemotype(s); the largest holds 46 of 66 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 6 heavy atoms, about 38% of a typical molecule, and 91% of the set can be cut at it
the 6 shared framework atoms sit 0.3 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (65 of 66 carry them)
the chosen attenuation 5 is at the top of the grid: the search needed a value it was not offered, so widen it before believing the model
the aligned model is +0.275 in q2 against counts (95% interval +0.090 to +0.490) -- the frame does better than counts
the aligned model is +0.107 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.086 to +0.308) -- the frame gains nothing over invariant
the aligned model is +0.064 in q2 against topomer (95% interval -0.118 to +0.250) -- cutting the molecules and posing the pieces by rule does as well as the frame, on the molecules that can be cut
the aligned model is +0.254 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval +0.044 to +0.529) -- the geometry adds something

why: the frame carries signal and the molecules are superimposed, so a frame exists whoever made it; the several Murcko scaffolds only mean the program could not have built it, not that it is wrong
